seed: Objects of type `player` under action ACTION3 with touching neighbours [portal] show mixed outcomes: x x3, no_change x2. Find the condition in the before state that decides the outcome. Start from this kind of condition: a global object such as a counter, HUD element or legend, read as state. Verify it against every transition before you keep it.

synth.notes:
Terrain read from frame colours: 2 = wall for all, 15 = wall for player only (blocks slide over it), 4 = socket border (passable inside socket bbox), off-board = wall.
Arrow moves player 3; if its next rect overlaps a token, the token is kicked instead and slides 3/step as a chain (absorbing hit tokens) until a member hits wall/player/non-fitting socket interior.
Click on a token: player takes its rect, token removed; tokens re-ranked token_i by (y,x). Stateless, no hidden state needed.
Hypothesis 'player A3 [portal] x vs no_change, global counter' = red herring: no_change is player at x30 facing colour-15 cells.
Unconfirmed: docking of an exactly-fitting token in a socket (tag change/stop) and whether colour-15 under objects matters.
